description: Framework-agnostic core for fluent log assertions over Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Testing.FakeLogCollector. Provides ILogRecordFilter + LogFilter composable filter primitives, the failure-message rendering, the FakeLogCollector inspection extensions (Filter, CountMatching, DumpTo), event-driven waits for background logs (WaitForLogAsync, WaitForLogsAsync on FakeLogCollector.GetLogsAsync), the LogCollectorBuilder factories (Create returns a LogCapture, CreateDiscarding), deterministic renderers for snapshot baselines (LogSnapshotRenderer for captured records, LogContractRenderer for log definitions), and a source generator that writes a LogDefinition for each [LoggerMessage] method of an opted-in assembly ([assembly: GenerateLogDefinitions(typeof(T))]). Test-framework-specific entry points live in adapter packages (LogAssertions.TUnit); adapters for other test frameworks are not planned, as the family targets TUnit.
releaseNotes:
View the rendered release notes: https://github.com/JohnVerheij/LogAssertions.TUnit/releases/tag/v0.17.0

### BREAKING

- **`LogDefinition.Properties`** was removed: a definition is the identity of a log call, and the argument values of a capture moved to `LogCall.Properties`. Migration: capture with `LogCall.Capture(...)` and read `call.Properties`; for the placeholder names alone, read `LogDefinition.PlaceholderNames`.
- **`LogDefinition.Exception`** was removed, for the same reason. Migration: `LogCall.Capture(...)`, then `call.Exception`.
- **`LogDefinition.Level`** changed from `LogLevel` to `LogLevel?`: a generated definition has no level when its method takes the level as a parameter. A captured definition still holds the level of the capture call. Migration: `definition.Level ?? ...`, or `definition.Level!.Value` where the definition is captured.
- **`LogDefinition.Template`** is `null` for an empty template: an empty template is no template. `LogDefinition.Capture` of a `[LoggerMessage]` method without a message used to return `""` (Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions writes an empty template; Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry writes none), and `LogContractRenderer.Render` and `LogDefinition.ToString()` wrote `""` for it; it now returns `null`, and both write `<no template>`. `Matching` treats an empty template and none alike. Migration: regenerate a contract baseline that holds such a method, and review the diff.
- **`LogFilter.MatchingCall`** takes a `LogCall` instead of a `LogDefinition`. A generated definition has no argument values, so passing one to the exact-call filter is a build error now, not a filter that never matches. The chain's `MatchingCall(log => ...)` is unchanged. Migration: `LogFilter.MatchingCall(LogDefinition.Capture(...))` becomes `LogFilter.MatchingCall(LogCall.Capture(...))`.

### Added

- **`[assembly: GenerateLogDefinitions(typeof(T))]`**: a source generator, shipped in the LogAssertions package, writes a `LogDefinition` for each `[LoggerMessage]` method of the assembly that contains `T`, at compile time and without reflection. For each type it adds an internal class `<Type>LogDefinitions` in the type's namespace with one field per method, so a test writes `HasLogged().Matching(OrderServiceLogDefinitions.LogOrderShipped)` without a capture lambda or throwaway arguments. A generated definition carries the identity the method's records carry, whichever of Microsoft's two logging generators compiled the product (Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions or Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry): the attribute's event ID, or, when it sets none, the ID the product's logging generator derives, as each version derives it (a hash of the event name; -1 before Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions 8.0; 0 before Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry 8.2; a hash of the C# text for the name in Telemetry 8.2 to 9.7); the event name as the record carries it (a backslash escape in it takes effect, with either generator), or the method name when it is empty or whitespace; the template as the record carries it (with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions before 11.0 a backslash escape in the message takes effect); and the placeholder names in the record's order, including the parameters the template does not use (with Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry, not a data-classified one). With Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry, a `[TagName]`, `[TagProvider]` or `[LogProperties]` parameter keeps its own name in `PlaceholderNames` (the first two are not compiled into the product, and the generator does not expand the properties of the third), and so, with Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions 8.0 and later, does a parameter of a referenced assembly written with an `@` its name does not need (a compiled assembly does not record it); matching is not affected. A project that references only LogAssertions.TUnit gets the generator too. The generator sees public and protected methods, and internal ones when the product names the test project in `InternalsVisibleTo`; a private method is not in the reference assembly a test project compiles against, and the generator applies the same rule to a project reference in an IDE, so the editor and the build agree.
- **`GenerateLogDefinitionsAttribute`** (with `TypeInAssembly`): the assembly attribute that opts a product assembly in, named by any type in it; apply it once per product assembly.
- **Generator warnings `LOGA001` to `LOGA004`**, reported at the `GenerateLogDefinitions` attribute: an opted-in assembly has no `[LoggerMessage]` method the test project can see; two methods of a type share a name, so neither gets a definition; two types would generate the same class, so neither does; a generated name is taken (a type the test project sees, or a namespace, already has the class's full name, a type the test project sees has the full name of one of its namespaces, or a method is named like the class), so it is left out.
- **`LogDefinition.Create(EventId, LogLevel?, string?)`**: builds a definition from its parts, reading the placeholder names from the template, for a record whose logging code a test cannot call.
- **`LogDefinition.Create(EventId, LogLevel?, string?, IEnumerable<string>)`**: the same with the placeholder names as given. The generated definitions use it.
- **`LogDefinition.PlaceholderNames`**: the names of the placeholder values a record of the definition carries.
- **`LogCall`**: one captured log call, `LogCall.Capture(log => ...)`, with its `Definition`, `Properties`, and `Exception`, for `LogFilter.MatchingCall`.

### Changed

- **`LogContractRenderer.Render`** writes `?` as the level of a definition without one (a generated definition whose method takes the level as a parameter). Lines of captured definitions are unchanged.
- **README:** a section on the generated definitions, and the recommendation to give each `[LoggerMessage]` method an explicit `EventId`, so a renamed method keeps its event ID.
